new_scholarship.name: VU Fellowship Programme (VUFP)
new_scholarship.description: The VU Fellowship Programme (VUFP) is VU Amsterdam's own merit-based tuition fee waiver for talented prospective non-EU/EEA students pursuing a full-time English-taught Master's degree at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Applicants must hold a bachelor GPA equivalent to a Dutch 8, already hold a conditional or unconditional admission for a September 2027 start, and prove academic excellence with a transcript and grading scale. The VUFP covers the tuition fees only and provides no allowance towards rent, food or insurance; the 2027/2028 application window opens 1 November 2026 and closes 1 February 2027 at 23:59 CET. Applying for the VUFP also applies the applicant for the separate NL Scholarship, a EUR 5,000 living-cost contribution awarded to only a small number of winners.

new_scholarship.name: Erasmus Trustfonds Scholarship
new_scholarship.description: The Erasmus Trustfonds Scholarship is funded by the Erasmus Trustfonds, a fund founded to support research and education projects organised by Erasmus University Rotterdam. It awards up to EUR 17,500 for one academic year towards the statutory tuition fee, housing and living costs to high-achieving incoming Master's students who cannot finance their own study. The award is administered by the university's participating schools - ESL, ESSB, ESHCC, ESHPM, RSM, ESE, ESPhil and EMC - each of which sets its own eligibility, documents and deadlines. For the 2026-2027 round the application has closed and information for 2027-2028 is expected in the autumn.

new_scholarship.description: The Lutfia Rabbani Scholarship Fund is intended for students who have demonstrated exceptional academic excellence and a strong motivation to promote Euro-Arab dialogue. Funded through a partnership established in 2018 between the Lutfia Rabbani Foundation and the Leiden University Fund, it awards EUR 30,000 for one academic year. The Willem F. Duisenberg Fellowship Foundation, established in 2007 in honour of Willem F. Duisenberg and supported by De Nederlandsche Bank, the Dutch Ministry of Finance, ING Group, Rabobank Nederland, ABN AMRO and AEGON, offers one five-month and one ten-month fellowship per academic year. Applicants need a minimum of three years of post-PhD academic experience; the fellowship targets prominent mid- to late-career researchers while encouraging exceptionally talented early-career candidates. Fellows receive a personal stipend, or a Dutch University Grant paid to their institution if affiliated with a Dutch university, plus an office, research facilities and subsidised accommodation where eligible. The 2027-2028 call ran from 15 January to 13 April 2026 and is now closed.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you have at least three years of post-PhD academic experience
Check that your work sits in applied monetary economics, macroeconomics, macroeconomic policy or public finance
Draft a full project proposal within 1,500 words including footnotes, excluding references and abstract
Prepare an up-to-date CV
Address in the proposal how your research would both benefit from and contribute to the NIAS community, since the Foundation asks for this reflection
Decide whether you want the five-month or ten-month fellowship, since one of each is offered per year
Establish whether you are affiliated with a Dutch university or research institute, as that changes the funding route to a grant paid to your institution
Plan to be in Amsterdam four working days a week for the semester
Note the call window: it opens in January and closes in April in the calendar year before the funded academic year, so watch for the early-2027 window for 2028-2029
common_rejection_risks: Fewer than three years of post-PhD academic experience
A project outside applied monetary economics, macroeconomics, macroeconomic policy or public finance
A proposal over 1,500 words, or one that counts references or the abstract toward the limit when the page excludes them
Missing the April closing date of the call window
Assuming the call opens in the autumn; it opens in January of the year before the academic year funded
Being unable to commit to four working days a week in Amsterdam
Expecting a published euro figure, which NIAS does not provide
Being passed over in favour of a more senior applicant, since the fellowship is primarily aimed at prominent mid- to late-career researchers
estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel to the Netherlands and back, which the page does not mention as covered
Visa and residence permit costs
Family or dependants' costs associated with a five- or ten-month relocation
Research expenses, fieldwork and conference travel
Anything beyond the stipend if a Dutch University Grant is paid to the institution instead
